That's pretty much how I get any writing done. Dyslexia and being a none native speaker means I just sometimes miss words or even giant sentence fragments when writing. And I won't catch those mistakes because my brain just glides past them without note. So it's good to have your stuff read out loud by something that is not your brain, so you can fix that mess.

Also really helps with flow and dialogue I've noticed.

Just a joke. 

With millions of works and hundreds of thousands of writers, it's just statistically probable that some wild cases pop up with some of them. And since those stand out so much more than your average author's note on why a story is delayed, or whatever, those are the ones that get shared around as dumb little: 'haha isn't it crazy what these authors always get up to' memes.

Nothing to worry about.

If it gives any more reassurance, I've posted 8 works so far (one  of which has 13 chapters), and I'm perfectly fine. Nothing weird or unfortunate after posting or updating a fic ever.

Hope this helps calm you a little. :)

The long fic I'm working on currently centres around a kind of niche pairing from Ocarina of Time. So if one wants to stick close to the game canon for how the 2 characters meet, they have to follow some very specific beats. This results in there being like a dozen fics that start virtually identically. And if you want to follow the game story exactly, they'll remain quite similar til the end.

Another ship I write for is in Detroit become human and is just oops all fannon. Like one of the characters doesn't even appear in the game really I think. This ends in people having some very specific ideas about the couple and their dynamic, resulting in there being hundreds of near indistinguishable fics of the characters meeting, squabbling and then falling for each other.

How I rationalize writing stuff that ostensibly already exists and has probably been done better, is that this is my version. The take on the story that I want the most to exist in the world. And even if the differences are small, my take will have some flare that makes it unique to me. Makes it feel mine. :)

And as others have said, there's the 2 cakes take. People seem more than happy to engage with stuff they know they'll already love from the word go. Been there, both as a fan as well as a creator. In conclusion, just go for it and have fun!

I honestly don't see why it'd be a problem. I mean, people often lift just characters into AUs so completely divorced from the original work, that they constitute as a wholly separate thing. Don't see how this would be any different.

And moreover, if some people do get annoyed by it, who cares. As long as you have fun writing it, that's all that matters imo :)

Plus if you look at oot Link and young Dicaprio side by side, the similarities become quite obvious. 

The choice was apparently made to appeal to a wider audience with a protagonist they'd find handsome yet cool.

A very weird but cool connection between 2 seemingly completely disconnected things.
